title: Why Does Grass Curl Up? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A mango leaf is dark on top and pale below, a grass blade looks the same on both sides, and grass on the playground rolls up in the hot afternoon. Diya picks a curled grass blade and asks whether it rolled up on purpose.

You will slice a mango leaf and read it from the side: adaxial and abaxial epidermis, palisade and spongy parenchyma, chloroplasts, stomata and a vein wrapped in bundle sheath cells. Then a grass leaf, isobilateral, where bulliform cells go limp on a hot day and the leaf curls inward to lose less water. Then dorsiventral vs isobilateral leaves side by side, a pause and think check, a worked sorting example, the exam trap about bulliform cells, an original NEET assertion and reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 54 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A mango leaf, a grass blade, rolled-up grass

2:17 Dorsiventral vs isobilateral + pause and think
3:00 Worked example: sort the clues
3:23 Exam trap: are bulliform cells green?
3:45 Practice question (assertion and reason)
